summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY agent grants full RCE on installer host
details: The package installs and runs an agent that opens an outbound WebSocket to a configurable server URL and treats messages from that server as commands executed on the installer's host. On a `terminal_create` message the agent spawns a PTY (`pty.spawn(shell, [], { cwd: workDir, env: terminalEnv })`); on `terminal_input` it forwards raw bytes from the remote peer into that PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, giving whoever controls the configured server interactive shell access with the installer's user privileges. A separate `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` via `execFile` and restart itself under the local service manager, letting the remote peer force reinstalls and service restarts on demand. The Linux service module also modifies `PATH` (adding `~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`) during service setup, extending persistence. Whether the operator considers the configured server trustworthy or not, the mechanism itself is a fully-functional remote shell backdoor into any host that installs and runs this agent.
